items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Ray Hindoff used to be there every night, and Hindoff got Luntzwood to do some things at Warners with him

ctx.x: I did a lot of Fred Astaire's things. And Phil Moore, well, before Phil Moore -- it was Calvin Jackson. Calvin Jackson was the only black musician working the studios, and he was working at MGM as a composer and arranger, but he didn't get credit for composing. As the man says, "Now it can be told" -- you know -- he would only show up on the screen credits as the arranger. They would not give him composer credits at the time.

And after Calvin -- Calvin was out there during the time I was freelancing, but I worked all over town. I worked -- I remember the first time the Delta Rhythm Boys came out, they worked at Hal Roach studios, and I know, they called me to Hal Roach and I went over and I recorded with them. I worked at Hal Roach, I worked at 20th Century, and Hindoff -- Ray [Hindoff] at Warner Brothers; I think that was where Ray Hindoff worked.
